representing the National Highway Authority of India (hereinafter for short 'the NHAI'),
2.

The petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs:
Deepak Kumar Shahi vs The Union Of India on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173436332/
1 (i) for issuance of a writ in the nature of writ of certiorari or any Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 other appropriate writ, order or direction for setting aside Letter bearing No.781 dated 13.04.2023 (Annexure- P/8) issued by the Respondent No.6 i.e., the District Land Acquisitions Officer Muzaffarpur without jurisdiction being 'FUNCTUS OFFICIO' after declaration and passing of award dated 21.01.2023, whereby it has been informed to the petitioner that the compensation already determined and declared with the prevailing rate of the commercial land against the acquired land of the petitioner could not be paid at the rate of the commercial type of land;
(ii) for issuance of a writ in the nature of writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction commanding the respondents specifically respondent Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 no.6 to pay compensation as calculated and determined amounting to Rs.31,31,789/- vide award dated 21.01.2023 passed by the respondent no.6 against the acquired land of the petitioner pertaining to Plot No. 1008 Area 0.0021 hectare situated in Mauza Madhuban Jagdish alias Bajhila alongwith applicable interest as per section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013, herein after called Act 30 of 2013;
(iii) for any other relief or reliefs which the petitioners may be found entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.
3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he has purchased a piece of land from Ram Dayal Sah, the land Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 holder.
The plot no. is 1008 in Madhuban Jagdish which comes under the jurisdiction of the District Land Acquisition Officer, Muzaffarpur (respondent no.6).

According to him, on 16.2.2022, a gazette notification was issued relating to acquisition of land in showing it as 'Bhith' land in the district of Muzaffarpur for the widening of NH-77 (Hajipur-Muzaffarpur) and the aforesaid plot no. 1008 was part of it.
It is his submission that in the subsequent notification dated 23.6.2022 (Annexure-P/3), they themselves recorded it as a commercial land.
He has further taken this Court to the committee's report of 19.5.2022 which included amongst other the District Land Acquisition Officer, Muzaffarpur in which again it was shown as commercial land.

4. Learned counsel submits that later they prepared Award taking into account the land to be commercial duly signed by their District Land Acquisition Officer, Muzaffapur on 21.1.2023 (Annexure-P/5).
5.

However, vide letter dated 13.4.2023 (Annexure- P/8), the District Land Acquisition Officer,
Muzaffarpur informed him that considering the nature of the land, on the date of notification,
commercial rates cannot be extended to the petitioner.
The submission is that once the process was completed, an Award prepared, the competent authority could Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 not have reverted himself.

8. He has relied on a learned Single Judge order of this High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam in the case of Usman Arif vs. the Project Director, N.H.A.I. and others [WP(c) 1996 of 2021] in which paras 11 to 12 read as follows:
11. the powers and competence of CALA are clearly specified, enumerated and detailed in the N.H. Act.

sentences.text: As per Section 3G thereof, where any land is acquired under Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 the Act, there shall be paid an amount to be determined by the CALA.

The said Authority is empowered and authorised to make such determination with respect to the value of the acquired land in terms of Section 3G(7) of the Act and then Section 3G(5) provides that if either of the parties is dissatisfied with the amount so arrived at by the CALA, they can seek it to be determined by the Arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government;

12. it is thus incontestable that upon the CALA determining the amount under Section 3G of the Act and issuing the resultant Award, he is rendered functus officio and cannot, thereafter, assume any further Statutory jurisdiction with respect to the same.

The CALA can, at the Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2)
dt.10-05-2024 best, correct patent typographical or clerical errors, but is proscribed from dealing with the published Award on its merits, in any manner, thereafter.

Therefore, by no means can the CALA modify his earlier Award or attempt to do so and any step in such direction by it will have to be declared as being without legal competence;
13.
that being so said, there is no doubt it being admitted that the Awards in question were settled on 27.12.2019; while Annexure Rl (a) instructions were issued by the NHAI only on 11.08.2020.

Therefore, even if it is taken for the sake of argument that the CALA is bound by the same, I fail to understand how the said Authority could have reviewed or attempted to review the Awards passed prior to Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 it, as has been done through the Impugned proceedings,

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of 'the NHAI' on the other hand submits that a bare perusal of the order in question would show that the reason has been given inasmuch as the nature of the land has to be taken as recorded in the Revenue Record on the date of publication of section 3A notification.

As the notification of land in question took place on 27.2.2022 in which it was shown 'Bhith' land on the basis of the subsequent conversion into commercial one on 16.4.2022, the payment could not have been extended and the DLAO, Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2)
dt.10-05-2024 Muzaffapur rightly passed the order.

10. He submits that in any case, 'the NHAI' has already moved before the District Judge,
Muzaffarpur in L.A. Case No. 13/2023 which came to be disposed of on 14.9.2023 directing the petitioner to go before the said office.

11. He further took this Court to Annexure-P/12 to the notice vide memo no. 2470 dated 31.10.2023 to show that though the petitioner chose to skip, the respondent did abide by the order of learned District Judge, Muzaffarpur and noticed him.
He submits that though there is statement in para-26 that he appeared on 11.11.2023, no document is on record.

He as such submits that when pursuant to an order of learned District Judge, Muzaffarpur, the District Land Acquisition Officer,
Muzaffarpur is already having the case pending before his office, there was no necessity for the petitioner to rush to Patna High Court in a writ jurisdiction and as such the writ petition is fit to be dismissed.

delivered in the different facts and circumstances in no case can be made applicable in the present case.
17. The petitioner in the opinion of this Court has definitely rushed to the High Court in writ jurisdiction when his petition pursuant to the order of the learned District Judge, Muzaffarpur in L.A. No. 13/2023 is still pending and it is reiterated that there is no supplementary affidavit to show Deepak Kumar Shahi vs The Union Of India on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173436332/
6 that the said matter has been taken to its logical conclusion.

11. He further took this Court to Annexure-P/12 to the notice vide memo no. 2470 dated 31.10.2023 to show that though the petitioner chose to skip, the respondent did abide by the order of learned District Judge, Muzaffarpur and noticed him.
18. Considering the aforesaid facts, although, the writ petition is fit to be dismissed, as his case is pending before the Patna High Court CWJC No.1717 of 2024(2) dt.10-05-2024 District Land Acquisition Officer, Muzaffarpur (respondent no.6), the said respondent is directed to take the case of the petitioner [pursuant to the office notice/memo no. 2470 dated 31. 10.2023 (Annexure-P/12)] to its logical conclusion, if still not concluded preferably within a period of four months from the date of the receipt of the copy of the order.
19.
